decimalHandling.what_prime_decimals_aware_means: Unlike BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook (no scale; assumes 18-dp USDS) and NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook (hard-coded USDC_TO_PHUSD_SCALE=1e12 for fixed 6-dp), Uniboost reads the prime token's decimals() ONCE in the constructor and derives immutable scale = 10**(18 - d), so the same hook code is correct for any prime with decimals <= 18.
decimalHandling.debt_formula: added = (amount * scale * ratio) / 100  (amount in prime-decimals; result in phUSD 18-dp wei)
decimalHandling.rounding: multiply-then-divide, floors -> sub-wei dust accrues to protocol, never over-credits. Direction matches NudgeRatchet's documented safe direction.
decimalHandling.verified_correct_against_M03_trap: Scale is in the CORRECT direction (multiply UP by 10**(18-d)), matching NudgeRatchet's 1e12-multiply fix. This does NOT reproduce the M-03 sign-flip over-mint trap (which divided instead of multiplied / used wrong exponent). For 6-dp prime: 1e6 amount @ ratio 50 -> 1e6*1e12*50/100 = 5e17 wei phUSD = 0.5 phUSD per 1 USDC. Correct.
decimalHandling.decimals_gt_18: require(d <= 18) in constructor blocks the underflow that 18-d would cause for >18-dp tokens. Tokens with d>18 (rare) are rejected at deploy, not mis-scaled.
potential_concerns_for_scanners: scale is fixed at deploy from the prime token passed to the HOOK constructor (primeToken_), NOT read live from the Uniboost dispatcher's primeToken(). If the hook's primeToken_ differs from the dispatcher's actual prime (mis-wiring at deploy), scale is wrong and debt is mis-scaled. No on-chain cross-check ties hook.scale to dispatcher.primeToken(). Flag.

DEFAULT_RATIO=50 and MAX_RATIO=50: setRatio allows newRatio==50 (only >50 reverts), so 50 is settable; constant comment says 'strictly < MAX_RATIO' but code is inclusive (newRatio > MAX_RATIO reverts). Comment/code mismatch (same as BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook). Cosmetic but note.
decimals() is read once; if the prime token were an upgradeable/rebasing token that changed decimals later, scale would be stale (standard ERC20 assumption holds, low concern).

hookWiring.no_hookTypeId: UniboostMintDebtHook does NOT expose hookTypeId() and IUniboostMintDebtHook does NOT declare it (contrast: NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook.HOOK_TYPE_ID + hookTypeId(), the M-04 fix). So even if Uniboost wanted to enforce the hook type, this hook provides no identity marker to check against.
hookWiring.onDispatch_gating: onDispatch is gated to the seeded/repointable `dispatcher` address (prevents external debt inflation). This is the inflation guard, NOT a wiring guard - it does not ensure the Uniboost dispatcher actually calls THIS hook.
hookWiring.footgun: Mirror of M-04: if the owner never wires this hook into Uniboost via setHook, the dispatcher keeps the NO-OP DefaultDispatchHook and accrues ZERO phUSD debt while still buy-and-pooling prime -> unbacked-value asymmetry. Neither contract self-detects the mis-wire.

localInvariants: mintDebt only increases via onDispatch(+=added) and is zeroed atomically in pull before the mint (CEI-ordered, nonReentrant)
pull callable only by owner or recipient; reverts if recipient==0; no-op if mintDebt==0
scale immutable, in [1, 1e18], derived from prime decimals in [0,18]
trustAssumptions: Hook holds minter authorization on phUSD (else pull reverts in phUSD.mint)
Owner wires the hook into Uniboost and sets recipient before relying on debt accounting
primeToken_ passed to constructor equals the dispatcher's real prime token (decimals must match for correct scale)
Owner is fully trusted (per repo Law 3) - repointable dispatcher/recipient add no new trust
redFlagsForScanners: DECIMAL: scale is correct-direction (multiply by 10**(18-d)); does NOT reproduce M-03 sign-flip over-mint. BUT scale is sourced from hook-ctor primeToken_ with no live tie to dispatcher.primeToken() - deploy-time mis-wire mis-scales all debt. Flag for code-scanner.
